# Recorded C550 validation

The implementation was validated with MACA 3.7.2, the SDK reporting LLVM 22.0.0git, MetaX plugin 0.6.2, and FlagTree runtime built from upstream `a246cf05a879d9aeed2cbef1d373aa3aa30a59c6`. The PR is based on the fork's `main` (`11e9e3415`); it does not import the 104 intervening upstream commits. The optional build selects plugin 0.6.2, while the default build retains the fork's plugin 0.6.1. A complete wheel rebuild from the fork's base remains untested.

## Compiler checks

- Standalone CMake build of `metax-mm-opt` passed.
- 36 prototype structural tests passed.
- 24 repository tests compile ordinary source fixtures and check the transform with index rematerialization enabled and disabled, including the long-K exception; no archived candidate IR is used as compiler input.
- All 51 repository-built JIT binaries matched the GPU-validated binaries: 48 selected routes and three additional edge cases.
- Default option parsing/cache identity work without the optional executable. Explicit optimization without the executable fails with a build instruction; shape/group/split options without the pipeline flag are rejected.

Reproduce the build and source-compile tests using the commands in [README.md](README.md), against the stated SDK/runtime. These tests do not launch GPU work.

## Full-suite measurements before index rematerialization

The frozen plan contains 42 non-split routes and six split-K routes generated by this compiler. Its other 72 routes retain earlier operator source/configuration tuning. These whole-plan measurements must not be interpreted as speedups from the compiler change alone. The full plan and benchmark records are retained in the task checkpoint; the 72 operator configurations are outside this compiler PR.

The upstream benchmark set contains 120 distinct `(M,N,K)` shapes and 121 configurations. Five alternating graph timing rounds were run per shape after freezing the plan. Timing includes both partial and reduction kernels for split-K, and excludes JIT, allocation, quantization, and baseline pre-dequantization.

| Reference time / optimized plan time | Distinct-shape arithmetic mean | Upstream-configuration-weighted mean |
|---|---:|---:|
| Native INT8 | 0.96181357 | 0.96173603 |
| BF16 GEMM | 1.67246404 | 1.67239475 |

Native `(4096,1,152064)` was not rerun after a previously observed native memory violation; the native comparison covers 119 distinct shapes. BF16 covers all 120. Twenty selected shapes still spill. Mean targets are met; this does not establish a per-shape win.

All 120 shapes passed bounded random full-output checks with TF32 disabled, two full-range INT8 seeds (`17`, `20260921`) with up to 64 CPU INT64 reference samples per seed, three constant extreme-input full-output checks, output guards, and captured-graph replay after replacing input values. The six split routes additionally passed per-part INT32 checks against CPU INT64 samples.

Frozen dispatch SHA256: `45f20c0990be980248f61e668d093fa35aa6536a00d6b089f69ed905980a7b78`.

The original runtime, `libtriton`, prebuilt MetaX plugin, and native library were left unchanged. The compiler transform and repository integration were tested through an isolated backend.

## Index rematerialization follow-up

Inspection of final MIR for representative spilling kernels found private-memory stores before the steady-state loop and reloads in the peeled tail. The values were thread-derived indices and output-related indices. This was not repeated accumulator spilling in every loop iteration. Runtime spill counts also include a fixed frame slot, so they need not equal the number of explicit spill-store instructions.

With `experimental_mm_rematerialize_indices=True`, all 51 source-generated candidates passed bounded full-output references, two full-range INT8 seeds with exact full-output comparison to the prior compiler binary and CPU INT64 samples, three full-output extreme cases, guards, and changed-input graph replay. All 20 previously spilling selected routes reached zero spills. However, `(1848,1536,128256)` repeatedly became roughly 2–5% slower in the initial paired reruns, despite eliminating its spills. Later probes also reproduced the regression. Its main-loop opcode order was unchanged after removing physical register names; the physical allocation changed. These results do not establish a hardware register-bank-conflict diagnosis.

The retained plan therefore enables rematerialization on 47 of the 48 compiler routes and keeps the remaining long-K binary byte-for-byte unchanged. The option is disabled by default; this per-route choice belongs to the measured plan, not a shape exception embedded in the compiler. The selected spill count falls from **20 to 1**. Across the 48 routes, the seven-round paired old-time/new-time mean is **1.00160393×**, which should be treated as essentially unchanged performance. The three additional edge cases are outside that mean.

The final backend rebuilt all 51 cases from ordinary Triton source: 50 binaries matched the already validated rematerialized versions, and the long-K exception matched the old binary. No recorded LLVM IR was used as the source input. The 72 operator/configuration routes and all split-K factors remain unchanged. Experiments with alternative identity representations, register-allocation flags, delayed shared loads, and split-K=3 for the long-K case were not retained.

Final dispatch SHA256: `b65d3e761146d80e3518a6e199ca80b42896042bac24bc1b6bbf5655a98566bf`.

The final standalone CMake build and all **24 repository tests** passed (149.92 seconds). The frozen 120-shape rerun passed all numerical checks, guards, and changed-input graph replay, and independently confirmed **one** selected shape with spills. Five alternating graph timing rounds gave:

| Reference time / final plan time | Distinct-shape arithmetic mean | Upstream-configuration-weighted mean |
|---|---:|---:|
| Native INT8 | 0.96048006 | 0.96037436 |
| BF16 GEMM | 1.66747736 | 1.66736500 |

Both mean targets still pass. The previously failing native `(4096,1,152064)` was again excluded. These are whole-plan measurements, including the same 72 retained operator/configuration routes; differences between separate full-suite runs are not a controlled measurement of compiler-only gain. The paired measurement above is the relevant comparison for this follow-up. A complete wheel rebuild from the fork's base remains untested.
